elements.element: Renewal by mutual written agreement OR automatic renewals of 12-month duration
elements.evidence: "will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms"; initial term is "one (1) year"

elements.element: Customer may opt out of automatic renewal on 30 days' notice
elements.evidence: "or elect not to renew the then-current Term, for any reason following the Initial Term upon thirty (30) days written notice"

elements.element: Vendor reminder notice 60 days before each renewal
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation anywhere in the redlined clause; nothing requires Kubient to notify Customer before renewal.

elements.element: Renewal price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%
elements.evidence: Clause is silent on renewal pricing; no cap language inserted (official check: "preferred automatic renewal includes the lesser-of-CPI-and-3% price cap" — not met).
"This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms"

elements.element: Non-renewal notice window no more than 60 days
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days written notice to the other Party" — 30 days is within the 60-day outer limit
No pricing cap in the clause; renewal pricing left entirely uncontrolled.

reasons: Target level is preferred, but two preferred atomic elements are absent: the 60-day Vendor reminder before each renewal and the lesser-of-CPI-and-3% cap on renewal price increases. The playbook's precision position requires stating the renewal price cap for automatic renewal even where the original is silent, so silence does not excuse it here.

The notice-window element is completed: 'ninety (90)' became 'thirty (30)' and the sentence expressly operates as a non-renewal election, satisfying the preferred 30-day exit (and comfortably inside the 60-day fallback outer limit). The deterministic 'number not found by literal pattern' result appears to be a pattern-matching artefact; the operative 'thirty (30) days written notice' is present in the rendered text.
Fallback is likewise incomplete because no ≤5% renewal price cap exists, so the clause cannot be treated as sitting acceptably at the fallback on price.

Fix minimally: append to the renewal sentence a short insertion such as 'Kubient shall notify Customer at least sixty (60) days before the end of the then-current Term, and fees for any renewal Term shall not increase by more than the lesser of CPI and 3% over the prior Term.' No other wording needs to change.

Minimality and intent are satisfied: only the notice number and a short clarifying phrase confirming the non-renewal election were changed; the cure period, insolvency right, and the Kubient fee-entitlement sentence remain untouched and effective, with no undefined terms introduced.
